Set a scratch SYNC_ENGINE_CACHE (one for each consumer) and REPO_SYNC_NO_AUTOUPDATE=1, and use MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS and symlinks of gomplate, dprint and pre-commit in a scratch bin folder on PATH, as the K1 run of the repo-sync-check plan did. Run mise run setup:configs in the first with SYNC_ENGINE_URL set to a local clone of main, and in the second with SYNC_ENGINE_URL set to a local clone of the run's branch. Then run diff -r on the two trees without .git.
keeps.pass: Both runs exit 0. The only differences are the bootstrap_commit line of .config/bootstrap.toml: no tool of bootstrap uses the new tables yet, so every rendered file is the same.

release_levels.reason: A [tools.<name>] table accepts values, and the templates get .config and .all. This is new behavior; a values file that works today works unchanged.

Tests: values, questions and contributions

decisions.decision: Does the plan need a review unit?
decisions.ruling: Yes. U1 adds sync-engine/values and changes sync-engine/repo-sync, and U2 changes a test task. Both are runnable bash. One review unit in wave 3 covers U1 and U2.
decisions.rejected: No review unit; the wave review alone does not run /security-review.

decisions.decision: Why is this plan in one linear chain with the other plans of the merge?
decisions.ruling: The 16 plans form one linear chain through requires. Most of them edit sync-engine/repo-sync or sync-engine/setup-sync, and parallel plans conflict there.

decisions.decision: Where do the tests of the new rules go?
decisions.ruling: This plan extends test:repo-sync with cases for its new rules. An existing case changes only where a ruling changes its expected result.

decisions.decision: Who runs mise run setup:configs in bootstrap and in the consumers?
decisions.ruling: The user, by hand, after the landing. It is out of scope, as in the earlier plans.
decisions.rejected: A unit or an after-landing step runs setup:configs.

decisions.decision: Which list rules apply to the [tools.<name>] values of a base or dependency tool?
decisions.ruling: Port the rules of setup-sync as they are. A base or dependency tool is a tool that pack base adds, also through a nested default = true pack ("pack:security": gitleaks, grype, osv-scanner, and _security_base through depends), or a tool in the depends closure of a selected tool, a tool that a mise depends adds included; a <tool> = {} member that the pack does not add does not count. It is a base or dependency tool also when a [tools.<name>] table names it. For such a tool, a list in [tools.<name>] appends its new items, and a value whose type differs from the merged value stops the sync with code 2. For any other tool, a value of [tools.<name>] replaces the merged one, and tables merge key by key.

decisions.decision: Is the env key of a [tools.<name>] table a value?
decisions.ruling: No. env stays the selection key of the repo side (a list, as today) and is not in .config. Every other key of [tools.<name>] is a value. A [packs.<name>] table keeps env as its only key.

decisions.decision: Does the repo side check that each question has an answer?
decisions.ruling: No. The engine validates only the shape of [questions]. A template that needs an answer uses required and fails that file with its message. Exit 4 stays Mac-only.
decisions.rejected: Exit 2 for a question with no value in [tools.<name>] and no default.

decisions.decision: How does each template get the .config of its own tool?
decisions.ruling: _rs_context adds .all (each selected tool name to its values, an empty table for a tool without values) to the shared context. For each tool that has a .tmpl file, the engine writes one context file: the shared context plus config, the values of that tool. config and all are engine keys, so they win over a top-level key of the same name in the values file, as members and tools do today.

decisions.decision: Does repo_sync --check examine the new tables?
decisions.ruling: No. [defaults], [questions] and [contributes] are in the tools.toml files of the clone, so they are clone rules, and only the sync examines them. --check keeps its local rule for [tools.<name>]: env, when present, is a list; any other key is now valid.
decisions.rejected: --check reads the clone to examine them.

decisions.decision: How do the values messages and codes read on the repo side?
decisions.ruling: A contribution to a tool that bootstrap does not have gives the message <tools root>/<tool>/tools.toml: [contributes.<x>] names a tool that bootstrap does not have, with the path from the tools root variable (repo/tools). The library logs every message and returns the highest code, as the sync does.
decisions.rejected: Stop at the first message; keep the macos-setup wording.
